hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are in a proper mood after the Women's team had their 20-game unbeaten run snapped by Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. The Slegers Out brigade are mobilising with complaints about tactics, substitutions and a lack of ideas in the final third — eerily similar to the men's team's woes. On the men's side, it's counting down the 13 days until Premier League return while enjoying the schadenfreude of City's 115 charges. The commentary on the Scotland match was apparently so bad it drove people to mute and sync radio feeds instead.

daily.summary: The day began with resigned acceptance of Manchester City's legal maneuvering (4/10), spiked into gleeful schadenfreude over the 115 charges mid-morning (8/10), then settled into a fatalistic, cynical groove by afternoon as focus shifted to Arsenal's own injury crisis and transfer frustrations (5/10 → 4/10). The City saga dominated throughout, but the brief schadenfreude high gave way to the fanbase's default setting: gallows humor and expectation of the worst.

weekly.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment traced a dramatic boom-and-bust arc across the week: cautious optimism early on built into bullish, title-chasing euphoria by mid-week, only to implode catastrophically after a 3-0 loss at Brighton on the 19th. The final two days saw sentiment plummet from peak confidence (8/10) to meltdown and despair (3/10), with Arteta's 'lack of respect' critique, exposed defensive frailties, and extinguished title hopes defining a thoroughly miserable finish.
